done.why: I ran out of turns, which is how this one ended. I'd made my way back to the sleeping cyclops for a rematch with the thief and was standing at the foot of the stairs to his hideaway. I had just typed "up" when the world said I'd used all 250 turns. Most of my turns went into mapping the maze, twice over.

about: It's the white house and the caves under it, with the far reaches closed off. Every way out of the middle caves ends in black water, a cave-in, or a dam "closed for inspection." So the place narrows to one path: kill the troll, get through the maze, feed and water the cyclops, and climb up to where a tidy, smug thief keeps his hoard. The thief is everywhere. He picks up what you drop, remarks on it from a distance, piles it in a dead end, and even puts your lamp back after you die. In the end it's a game about a burglar who keeps house.

ending.what: I got as far as the Treasure Room and fought the thief once. He killed me. I came back, got my things together, and had just reached the sleeping cyclops again when my turns ran out.

moments.note: The gothic lettering translates to "This space intentionally left blank." Good dry joke.
The air down the passage "smells faintly of something that has not bathed". The troll gets announced before I ever see him.
The troll description: "watching you the way a cook watches a chicken", with teeth "not all of them his own".
The cave-in rubble is sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest. Somebody tidy lives down here, and that sets up the thief.
The crack is "too narrow for most insects."
The Chasm description mentions a crack opening into a passage, but "examine crack" said there was no such thing.
"take bag and key" took only the key. The game read "bag" as the brown sack I was already carrying and ignored the leather bag of coins.
The rusty knife: "The rust has not touched the edge. That is not a thing rust usually overlooks." A quiet, ominous line.
A distant voice: "My, I wonder what this fine lunch is doing here." The thief tidies up after me.
The maze is a long slog. Every room reads "Maze", some exits are one-way, and I spent dozens of turns mapping it by dropping things that the thief then picked up.
The thief's stash of my lunch and bottle turned up in a dead end, and it's what I needed for the cyclops.
The cyclops takes the bottle and "checks that it's open". Nice touch, since he'd gotten agitated when I first handed it over closed.
The thief killed me in four exchanges, and I had no chance to back off.
The death text: "somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room." It turns a penalty into characterization.
On my second visit the Cyclops Room didn't mention the cyclops at all. Only examining him showed he was there.

wished: To go around the cave-ins, cross the black water, or open the dam. Every edge of the map closed off with a nice sentence and nothing to do.
To examine the crack the Chasm description mentions.
Rooms in the maze with even a small difference in their descriptions, so I could find my way by reading rather than by leaving my things behind.
To pick up the leather bag of coins by calling it a bag.
To back away from the thief or bargain with him instead of fighting to the death in four swings.

lines.line: He is watching you the way a cook watches a chicken.
lines.why: Funny and threatening in one short sentence. It set the voice for the whole place.

lines.line: somebody has sorted the nearest of it into neat heaps, smallest nearest, the way some people tidy a room they have no intention of using.
lines.why: It plants the idea of a tidy someone long before the thief shows up.

lines.line: The air that comes down it is cold, and smells faintly of something that has not bathed.
lines.why: It announces the troll through smell, before he's in view.

lines.line: The rust has not touched the edge. That is not a thing rust usually overlooks.
lines.why: The best sentence I read. Understated, and it suggests something without saying it.

lines.line: Whatever he came into the maze looking for, the maze found him first.
lines.why: A well-turned epitaph for the skeleton.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: Even dying fit the thief's character.

lines.line: a black slot in the floor of the world, too deep for any light to find the bottom
lines.why: A striking image for the chasm.

lines.line: It smells of hot peppers from across the room, and of more hot peppers from closer to.
lines.why: The comic rhythm made me laugh.

fun.why: The troll fight, the Loud Room echo, feeding the cyclops, and the thief's voice drifting through the maze were all good fun. A long stretch of maze mapping and a quick death to the thief dragged it down.

engagement.why: The tidy-someone thread kept me curious from the heaped rubble to the thief putting my lamp back. I wanted to get back up those stairs.

difficulty.why: The cyclops puzzle was fair. The maze took far more turns than it was worth, and the thief killed me before I could react. Together they used up the session.

interestingness.why: Making the thief into a tidy housekeeper is a real idea, and it shows in the rubble, the dead-end stash, and the death text. Most of the blocked exits are written as little stories of their own.

prose.why: Whenever the writing is new rather than familiar, it's excellent: dry, precise, and funny, with real rhythm. The troll, the knife, the skeleton, the chasm, and the death text all stand out. The bare "Maze" rooms are the only flat stretch.
